name: MonarchRecoveryCodes
title: RecoveryCodes
wrapsNative: Rows of androidx.compose.material3.Text in the code style with androidx.compose.ui.text.VerbatimTtsAnnotation; MonarchCopyButton, MonarchButton, an Intent.ACTION_SEND share sheet, androidx.compose.material3.AlertDialog and MonarchCheckboxRow
summary: One-time recovery codes in a monospaced grid, with copy, save or share, an optional show and hide button, generate new codes behind a confirmation, and an acknowledgement for setup flows.
whenToUse: When two-step verification is set up or reviewed, to give the person their backup codes and make sure they saved them.
whenNotToUse: Not for a single secret such as an API key (use MonarchCopyButton beside the value) and not for one-time passcodes the person types (use MonarchOtpPinInput).
api: @Composable fun MonarchRecoveryCodes(codes: List<MonarchRecoveryCode>, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, heading: String? = null, initiallyRevealed: Boolean = true, showRevealToggle: Boolean? = null, onSave: ((String) -> Unit)? = null, onRegenerate: (suspend () -> Unit)? = null, onAcknowledge: (() -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchRecoveryCodesLabels = MonarchRecoveryCodesLabels())
class MonarchRecoveryCode(code: String, used: Boolean = false)

class MonarchRecoveryCodesLabels(listLabel: String? = null, remaining: ((left: Int, total: Int) -> String)? = null, used: String? = null, copy: String? = null, copied: String? = null, save: String? = null, reveal: String? = null, conceal: String? = null, concealedHint: String? = null, regenerate: String? = null, regenerateTitle: String? = null, regenerateDescription: String? = null, regenerateConfirm: String? = null, cancel: String? = null, regenerated: String? = null, acknowledge: String? = null, acknowledgeMissing: String? = null, continueTitle: String? = null)

options.name: codes
options.description: The codes. Used codes are struck through and not copied or saved.

options.name: heading
options.description: A first line for the copied and saved text, such as the product and account, followed by a blank line.

options.name: initiallyRevealed
options.description: Whether the codes are visible at first.

options.name: showRevealToggle
options.description: Whether the show and hide button is shown. By default when the codes start hidden.

options.name: onSave
options.description: Saves the text of the codes, for example with a CreateDocument launcher. Without it Save opens the system share sheet.

options.name: onRegenerate
options.description: Replaces the codes after a destructive confirmation; pass the new codes back through codes. The button is busy until it returns.

options.name: onAcknowledge
options.description: Runs when the person ticks "I have saved my recovery codes" and presses Continue. Neither is shown without it.

states.name: used codes
states.description: Struck through in the subtle text color, with "3 of 4 codes left" above the codes.

states.name: hidden
states.description: A hint replaces the codes until "Show codes" is pressed.

states.name: regenerating
states.description: The regenerate button shows its progress indicator and reads "Loading".

states.name: acknowledgement missing
states.description: Pressing Continue without the checkbox shows an error in the danger strong color and announces it.

appearance: Codes sit on a panel with the subtle background and subtle border roles, in the code type style. Buttons are Monarch buttons: ghost for show and hide, secondary for copy and save, danger for generate new codes, primary for Continue. The confirmation is a Material 3 AlertDialog on the raised background with its confirm text in the danger strong role. All colors are theme roles, so dark and high-contrast themes follow.
platformNotes: The web's Download becomes Save or share: by default the system share sheet (Intent.ACTION_SEND with the codes as text), from which the person can save to a file, a password manager or another app; onSave lets the app write a file with a CreateDocument launcher instead. iOS shares a named text file; Android shares text, so there is no fileName. The web's confirm dialog is a Material 3 AlertDialog. The parity map names a grid; the codes are rows of a Column with as many columns as fit, because a LazyVerticalGrid cannot sit in a scrolling screen. Copy marks the clip as sensitive, so Android 13 and later hide it in the clipboard preview. The revealed state is internal (initiallyRevealed), as on iOS. The codes are not selectable as text; Copy covers that.
accessibility: The codes are a traversal group named "Recovery codes".
Each code carries a verbatim text-to-speech annotation, so TalkBack spells it character by character.
A used code has the state "Used", so its state does not depend on the strike-through.
All actions are Monarch buttons with 48dp touch targets; the acknowledgement is a MonarchCheckboxRow, one checkbox element.
New codes are announced through a polite live region after regenerating.
A missing acknowledgement is shown as text and announced through the same live region.
edgeCases: The codes take as many columns as fit at 112dp each, scaled with the font size, so the largest font sizes show one column.
A new set of codes clears the acknowledgement; marking a code used does not.
When onRegenerate throws, the button stops its progress and nothing is announced; the app reports the failure.

examples.title: Setup step with acknowledgement
examples.template:
MonarchRecoveryCodes(
    codes = listOf({{codes.0}}, {{codes.1}}, {{codes.2}}, {{codes.3}}, {{codes.4}}, {{codes.5}}, {{codes.6}}, {{codes.7}}).map { MonarchRecoveryCode(it) },
    labels = MonarchRecoveryCodesLabels(save = {{labels.save}}),
    showSave = false,
    onAcknowledge = { /* go to the next step */ },
)
examples.code:
MonarchRecoveryCodes(
    codes = listOf("4f7k-29dm", "q8zt-mx41", "h2vc-0pla", "r6yn-3ke8", "w1bs-7dqj", "c5ug-9fhr", "m3xe-6tnw", "p0lo-2ziv").map { MonarchRecoveryCode(it) },
    labels = MonarchRecoveryCodesLabels(save = "Download"),
    showSave = false,
    onAcknowledge = { /* go to the next step */ },
)

examples.title: Reviewing codes, hidden at first
examples.code:
MonarchRecoveryCodes(
    codes = listOf(MonarchRecoveryCode("4f7k-2m9q"), MonarchRecoveryCode("8d3r-6t1w", used = true)),
    initiallyRevealed = false,
)
